paragraphs: A Mercedes-Benz M156 engine rebuild starts from £3,600, regardless of which of the six models it's fitted to — the price tier is set by the engine, not the badge on the boot. A full replacement engine and fitting service is also available.
Exact pricing depends on the condition of your existing engine and the parts required — submit your registration for a fixed-price quote within 30 minutes.

cards.title: Rebuilding Your
cards.body: Most engine suppliers sell you a used engine of unknown history and hope it matches. We rebuild the engine your Mercedes already has instead — strip it down, pressure-test it, and replace every worn or damaged component with updated OEM parts. You get a near-new engine with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty, without the compatibility risk of an unknown used unit. This is the option most M156 owners choose.

cards.title: Replacement
cards.body: If your existing engine is beyond economical repair, we also offer full engine replacement and fitting — sourced and fitted by our team, with the same 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.

cards.title: Used
cards.body: In some cases, a matched low-mileage used engine is the right call — particularly if you need your car back on the road quickly and your existing engine's damage is extensive. We can source and fit these too, though most owners who ask about used engines end up choosing a rebuild once they understand the compatibility risk a used unit carries.

options.body: "Reconditioned" is the term many owners search for when they mean the same thing as a rebuild — a full strip-down, inspection, and replacement of worn parts rather than a straight swap. If that's what you're after, our rebuild service is exactly that.
"Refurbished" often describes the same process from a different angle — restoring your existing engine to full working condition rather than replacing it outright. Our rebuild covers this.

Some owners specifically search for a "remanufactured" engine, expecting a unit rebuilt to original specification with updated components. That's consistent with what our rebuild service delivers, regardless of which of the six M156-equipped models you drive.

faqLeft.q: What is the Mercedes-AMG M156 engine?
faqLeft.a: The M156 is Mercedes-AMG's first fully in-house developed engine — a naturally aspirated 6.2-litre V8 produced from 2005 to 2014. It's fitted across six AMG models: C63, CLK63, CLS63, E63, ML63 and R63.

faqLeft.q: Which Mercedes-AMG models use the M156?
faqLeft.a: C 63 AMG (W204), CLK 63 AMG (C209), CLS 63 AMG (C219), E 63 AMG (W211/W212), ML 63 AMG (W164) and R 63 AMG (W251) — see the full applications table above for exact years.

faqLeft.q: Does the M156 differ between AMG models?
faqLeft.a: The base engine is the same naturally aspirated V8 across all applications. The specific ancillaries and vehicle-specific components differ, and pre-2012 engines have known head bolt differences. We match by registration/VIN before confirming any rebuild or replacement.

faqLeft.q: Is an M156 from one AMG model compatible with another?
faqLeft.a: Not automatically. Ancillaries, mounting, and vehicle-specific components all differ. We always confirm compatibility by registration/VIN.

faqLeft.q: How much does a Mercedes-AMG M156 engine rebuild cost?
faqLeft.a: Rebuilds start from £6,500, regardless of which model it's fitted to. Exact price depends on condition and parts required — submit your reg for a fixed-price quote.
Yes. We work on M156 rebuilds across every AMG model it's fitted to, replacing worn components including timing chain, camshaft adjusters, head bolts, bearings and gaskets as standard.

faqRight.q: Can you rebuild an M156 from a C63 AMG?
faqRight.a: Yes. The C 63 AMG (W204) is one of the most common M156 applications we see in the workshop.

faqRight.q: Can you rebuild an M156 from an E63 AMG?
faqRight.a: Yes. The E 63 AMG (W211/W212) is one of the applications we work on regularly.

faqRight.q: Do you supply used Mercedes-AMG M156 engines?
faqRight.a: Yes, in some cases a matched low-mileage used engine is the right option. Our team will advise honestly once we've matched your registration and understood your situation.

faqRight.q: Can you recover my Mercedes-AMG if the engine has failed?
faqRight.a: Yes — nationwide recovery is available from £70, and most vehicles are collected within a few hours of booking.

faqRight.q: How long does an M156 engine rebuild take?
faqRight.a: Most rebuilds are completed within 3-5 working days from the time your car arrives at our workshop.

faqRight.q: Is rebuilding better than fitting a used engine?
faqRight.a: For most M156 owners, yes. A rebuild removes the compatibility risk that comes with an unknown used unit's history and comes with a 12-month unlimited-mileage warranty.
